Section 1008 of the Great Lakes Fish and Wildlife Restoration Act of 1990 (16 U.S.C. 941f) is amended to read as follows:“SEC. 1008. REPORTS.“(a) In General.—Not later than December 31, 2011, the Director shall submit to the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report that describes—“(1) actions taken to solicit and review proposals under section 1005;“(2) the results of proposals implemented under section 1005; and“(3) progress toward the accomplishment of the goals specified in section 1006.“(b) Public Access to Data.—For each of fiscal years 2007 through 2012, the Director shall make available through a public access website of the Department information that describes—“(1) actions taken to solicit and review proposals under section 1005;“(2) the results of proposals implemented under section 1005;“(3) progress toward the accomplishment of the goals specified in section 1006;“(4) the priorities proposed for funding in the annual budget process under this title; and“(5) actions taken in support of the recommendations of the Great Lakes Regional Collaboration authorized under Executive Order 13340 (69 Fed. Reg. 29043; relating to the Great Lakes Interagency Task Force).“(c) Report.—Not later than June 30, 2007, the Director shall submit to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Resources of the House of Representatives the 2002 report required under this section as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of the Great Lakes Fish and Wildlife Restoration Act of 2006.”
.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the 'Public Access to Data' website and the references to soliciting proposals and the Great Lakes Regional Collaboration amount to public involvement. They do not: the section only requires reports to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government, and one-way posting of information on a website. Disclosure to the public is not consultation, and no outside party is given a comment period, hearing, advisory role, or right to sue over a federal decision.

opus.w: Subsections (a) and (c) require reports to congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. Subsection (b) requires the Director to post information on a website for the public. That is disclosure, not a chance for outsiders to comment on or shape a federal decision. The reference to the Great Lakes Regional Collaboration only asks for a report of actions taken in support of its recommendations; the section itself creates no new consultation process.

opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because subsection (b) makes information available to the public and mentions the "Great Lakes Regional Collaboration." That reading fails. Reports to congressional committees stay inside the federal government. Posting data on a public website is one-way disclosure, with no comment, hearing or consultation before a decision. The Collaboration is only mentioned as something whose recommendations the Director must report on.

qwen_chat.w: This section primarily mandates reports to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. Subsection (b) requires making data available on a public website, but this is passive disclosure rather than active consultation or coordination with the public before a decision is made. There are no comment periods, public hearings, or advisory committees involving outside parties described in this text.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that subsection (b) requires "Public Access to Data" via a website, which could be seen as a form of public participation or transparency. However, the definition of participation requires consultation, coordination, or interaction *before* a decision is made (e.g., comment periods, hearings, advisory boards). Merely publishing data or reports for public consumption is not "participation" in the decision-making process as defined here; it is disclosure. Furthermore, the primary actions in this section are reports to Congress (inside the government) and data publication. There is no mechanism for the public to influence the decisions through this section.
